# Project plan

## Preliminary work

We reviewed existing tutorial tools alongside registries and metadata schemas. [Community feedback](https://github.com/rstudio/learnr/issues/766#issuecomment-5944898742) helped us focus the project on common metadata and checks. Our prior teaching work includes [Hutchins's candidate genetic variants module](https://cfdetrainingcenter.github.io/candidate-genetic-variants/) and [Bharti's r-for-beginners lessons](https://github.com/samuelbharti/r-for-beginners).

## Schedule and working practices

| Period | Work and completion criteria |
|----------|----------------------------------------|
| Months 1–2 | Review the eight-field schema, map metadata from existing tutorials into pilot records, establish repositories and governance, and begin the example tutorials. |
| Months 3–5 | Implement the three adapters and `check_tutorial()`. Publish a capability table and common report format. Test valid examples and known failures. |
| Months 6–8 | Build registry ingestion and search. Publish `index.json` and the R search interface. Run the pilot records through the package and document author effort. |
| Months 9–10 | Pilot nominations and human review with external contributors. Test stale-entry handling and gather usability feedback. |
| Months 11–12 | Complete example tutorial and integration-template checks. Address high-priority feedback and release version 1.0 of the package, specification, and registry with maintenance guidance. |

We will work openly on GitHub, using issues and milestones to track progress and pull requests for code review. We will publish monthly updates and milestone reports and invite community feedback. Package tests will use testthat, with renv to reproduce software environments. We will publish documentation with pkgdown and distribute the package through R-universe where appropriate.

Code will use the MIT license. Newly authored content and documentation will use CC BY 4.0 where compatible with source obligations; adaptations will retain required attribution and licensing. We will share release announcements and integration guidance with R education communities.

## Budget and funding

**Requested budget: USD 10,000.** This funds 200 hours at USD 50/hour, allocated 60% to project lead Hutchins (120 hours; USD 6,000) and 40% to Bharti (80 hours; USD 4,000). No hardware, cloud, travel, or fee costs are included.

| Milestone | Hutchins (h) | Bharti (h) | Total (h) | USD |
|---------------------------|------------:|----------:|----------:|----------:|
| Minimal schema | 18 | 12 | 30 | 1,500 |
| Adapters | 30 | 20 | 50 | 2,500 |
| Validation package | 33 | 22 | 55 | 2,750 |
| Registry | 21 | 14 | 35 | 1,750 |
| Review, governance, and examples | 18 | 12 | 30 | 1,500 |
| Total | 120 | 80 | 200 | 10,000 |

If funding is reduced, the schema and validation tools can be used independently of the registry.

## Risks and maintenance

Adoption is the main uncertainty. Authors may find the schema burdensome if it duplicates metadata they already maintain. We will reuse existing metadata and use early consultation and the indexing pilot to measure author effort, then revise the requirements before finalizing version 1.0.

Engine changes could break adapters or expose differences in test coverage. We will document supported versions and browser or server requirements, and use the example tutorials to detect regressions.

We will document contribution and governance procedures so others can maintain the registry without relying on us for every change. Entries will name maintainers and retain source links, validation dates, and status. Scheduled checks and an archival policy will help contributors address stale resources.
